Verdict

Reviewed 28 Oct 2026 · next 26 Jan 2027

Best fit for Neo4j-style graph exploration: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 15.8M weekly downloads, 138 KB gzip. Layouts come via extensions; the React wrapper is stale, so use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper.

Current Reviewed version 3.34.4 Requirement: Graph visualization in a React application

Reasoning

  1. MIT with a public repository and SLSA provenance from .github/workflows/release.yml.
  2. Zero runtime dependencies; 6 MB install and 138 KB gzip for the core bundle.
  3. No OSV advisories for 3.34.4.
  4. Active: 3.34.4 published 2026-10-15, repository pushed 2026-10-27, 11.3k stars.
  5. Layouts are extensions (dagre, cose-bilkent, fcose), so the feature set matches the NVL layouts without the proprietary licence.
  6. Canvas renderer handles typical Neo4j result sizes; for very large graphs, Sigma is the fallback.

Caveats

  • react-cytoscapejs is stale (last release 2022, 45 open issues, no types). Use cytoscape directly with a ref, or maintain a thin wrapper.
  • Layout extensions are separate packages with their own maintenance and licences.
  • Canvas rendering is slower than WebGL above roughly 10k-20k visible nodes.
  • The package ships UMD/ESM/CJS bundles, so the unpacked size is larger than the bundled cost.

Decision context

Approved

cytoscape is the primary choice for Graph visualization in a React application. This package is classified as Adopted.

The NVL suite is denied: its LICENSE.txt limits use to Neo4j Aura or commercial Neo4j, it publishes no repository, carries no provenance and cannot be loaded by Node in either module system. 1.2.2 was checked separately: same licence and packaging, different layout stack, so the denial applies to both. Adopt Cytoscape.js as the primary renderer: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 138 KB gzip, and layouts via extensions. Use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper because react-cytoscapejs is stale. Adopt Sigma.js as the fallback for large graphs: MIT, WebGL, 110 KB gzip and active, but client-only (WebGL2) and without provenance; pair it with graphology and @react-sigma/core. Hold @antv/g6 (88 MB, 104 packages, 413 KB gzip, 333 open issues, no release in 90 days) and @xyflow/react (excellent node editor, but not an exploration or layout engine).
